_comment: ShellTerra BlackCommerceSD vendor directory. Seeds the 'vendors' collection. Source lists: the sandiego.org 'Black-Owned San Diego Businesses' article and the DoSD 'Black Owned Businesses in San Diego' list (last updated January 2026), both researched and verified September 11, 2026. Entries that failed verification are NOT in the vendors array; they are parked in _excluded with reasons. Read _research_notes before seeding.

_fields.slug: REQUIRED. kebab-case unique id. Drives the deterministic doc id (re-run safe) AND the logo filename (images/vendors/BlackCommerceSD/<slug>.png).
_fields.name: REQUIRED. Business display name.
_fields.category: REQUIRED-ish. One tag for grouping/filtering, e.g. Restaurant, Retail, Beauty, Health, Services, Arts, Professional, Nonprofit.
_fields.tagline: Optional. Short one-liner shown under the name.
_fields.description: Optional. 1-3 sentence blurb for the card / detail display.
_fields.logoUrl: Optional. Direct image URL. If omitted, the seeder falls back to images/vendors/BlackCommerceSD/<slug>.png (drop a file there), then to the shell image.
_fields.instagram: Optional. Handle (with or without @) or full URL.
_fields.address: Optional. Full street address; powers the map/directions button.
_fields.lat: Optional but needed for the map pin. Decimal degrees. VERIFY each pin in Google Maps before seeding.
_fields.neighborhood: Optional. e.g. Encanto, Downtown, Southeast SD.
_fields.featured: Optional bool. Featured vendors can sort to the top / get a badge.
_fields.events: Optional array of {title, date (YYYY-MM-DD), time ('H:M' 24h), description}. Populates the 'event list for that vendor' section. Leave [] for businesses with no scheduled events.

_verify_before_running: SHELL_ID in .env (or per-run override) must be 6aa3675074c02a7ab6c4
Every lat/lng below came from the US Census Bureau geocoder or published map data, NOT from Google Maps. Drop each pin in Google Maps and confirm it lands on the right storefront before seeding.
All 'verified' flags are false: no owner has confirmed their listing yet. Flip to true only after owner contact.
Read _research_notes. Four vendors carry open-status caveats (Lili Kouture, Fivespace, EDEN San Diego, Dancing Around The Oak Tree) and one has unconfirmed Black ownership (Kebab Craft).

Four vendors have no address or pin on purpose: Dirt Don't Hurt and Finesse Products are online only, Furlicious is mobile, SDAAMFA has no permanent gallery. Puzzle Pieces Marketing and Dancing Around The Oak Tree also have no pin because their only published addresses are a private mailbox and a private residence.
Manuelita Brown (Encinitas) and Arts-Rec Chula Vista are outside San Diego city limits but inside the county.
Do not seed anything from _excluded without re-verifying it first.

vendors.name: Chula Vista Brewery
vendors.tagline: South Bay craft beer, Black and veteran owned
vendors.description: Craft brewery and taproom opened in 2017 by Timothy and Dali Parker in downtown Chula Vista's Third Avenue Village. The kid and pet friendly taproom pours house IPAs, ambers and lagers, including the GABF bronze medal winning Browner Than Ivan brown ale, and runs weekly comedy and vinyl nights.

vendors.name: Muzita Abyssinian Bistro
vendors.tagline: Eritrean and Ethiopian family recipes on Park Blvd
vendors.description: A University Heights bistro serving Eritrean and Ethiopian dishes built on family recipes, from slow simmered stews to vegetarian platters, all eaten with injera. The kitchen runs split lunch and dinner service daily and also handles catering and private events.

vendors.name: Coop's West Texas BBQ
vendors.tagline: West Texas brisket, served till it sells out
vendors.description: Lemon Grove barbecue institution run by pitmaster Bradrick Cooper, smoking West Texas style brisket, ribs and links alongside cornbread, mac and cheese and other Southern sides. After closing the storefront in 2024 it came back on a weekend only schedule, serving Friday through Sunday until the meat runs out, with catering available midweek.
vendors.address: 2625 Lemon Grove Ave, Lemon Grove, CA 91945

vendors.name: Nomad Donuts
vendors.tagline: Globally inspired donuts and wood fired bagels
vendors.description: North Park donut shop run by Brad Keiller, making small batch artisanal donuts in rotating international flavors such as ube and Mexican chocolate, with a steady vegan selection. The shop also bakes wood fired bagels and serves breakfast sandwiches and coffee.

vendors.name: OneWorldBeat Cafe
vendors.tagline: Vegan Caribbean plates inside Balboa Park
vendors.description: A plant based cafe inside the WorldBeat Cultural Center in Balboa Park, serving vegan soul food and Caribbean inspired dishes made partly with produce from the center's garden. It offers pickup, outdoor seating and limited indoor dining on the center's weekend schedule.

vendors.name: Maya's Cookies
vendors.tagline: America's top Black owned vegan cookie company
vendors.description: Founded in 2015 by Maya Madsen, Maya's Cookies bakes soft gourmet vegan cookies in flavors like chocolate chip s'more and marble fudge, inspired by her travels and memories. The Grantville flagship anchors a business that also sells at San Diego County farmers markets and ships nationwide.
vendors.address: 4760 Mission Gorge Pl, Suite G, San Diego, CA 92120

vendors.name: Kebab Craft Mediterranean Grill
vendors.tagline: Cali Mediterranean kebabs, bowls and pitas
vendors.description: A Mediterranean and Middle Eastern grill at Booth 32 inside Liberty Public Market, opened in 2022 and built on family recipes shaped by Parisian training. The menu centers on build your own plates, bowls and pitas alongside signatures like the Cali Kebab, loaded fries and baklava.
vendors.address: 2820 Historic Decatur Rd, Booth 32, San Diego, CA 92106

vendors.name: Dirt Don't Hurt
vendors.tagline: Charcoal powered clean beauty from three SD sisters
vendors.description: An online brand launched by San Diego sisters Kaya, Sativa and Maritza Murray after searching for nontoxic products for their own families. The vegan, cruelty free line runs on activated charcoal, earth clays, essential oils and herbs across oral care, skin care and body care, sold direct and wholesale.

vendors.name: Lili Kouture
vendors.tagline: African fabric fashion, designed and sewn in City Heights
vendors.description: A woman and Black owned City Heights boutique run by designer Lalitibe Klu, who sews modern, easy to wear garments from cotton sourced in Togo and elsewhere in West Africa. The shop, also known as LK Fashion, sells dresses, separates and custom pieces across a wide size range.
vendors.address: 4274 El Cajon Blvd, San Diego, CA 92105

vendors.name: Fivespace
vendors.tagline: Hip hop vinyl, tapes and vintage
vendors.description: A North Park record shop founded by producer Sir Froderick, stocking hip hop and rap vinyl, cassettes and CDs alongside vintage apparel, pins, patches and books. It is known for rare titles, lathe cut records made on site and personal shopping appointments, and also sells through its own web store.
vendors.address: 2305 University Ave, Unit 101, San Diego, CA 92104
vendors.hours: Online store open 24/7, walk in hours unconfirmed

vendors.name: Freshly Faded Barber + Shop
vendors.tagline: Get in, get fresh, get out
vendors.description: A North Park barbershop founded by Derrick Banks, specializing in fades, tapers, beard work and hot towel straight razor shaves for adults and kids. The shop doubles as a community space stocked with local art, books, pins and vintage magazines, and hosts men's health talks, screenings and voter registration drives.
vendors.address: 2850 El Cajon Blvd, Suite 1, San Diego, CA 92104

vendors.name: Reggae World
vendors.tagline: North Park's longtime reggae shop and apothecary
vendors.description: Operating on University Ave since around 2000 under owner Zulu Miller, Reggae World sells reggae music, T shirts, bags, patches and jewelry. It is equally known for scented shea butters, body oils, incense and imported African goods, and keeps daily hours.

vendors.name: Common Ground Theatre
vendors.tagline: San Diego's longest running Black theatre company
vendors.description: Common Ground Theatre stages classic and new works by and about people of African descent at the Educational Cultural Complex Theatre in southeastern San Diego. Led by Executive Artistic Director Yolanda Marie Franklin, it completed its 62nd season in 2026 and puts particular weight on arts education for children and youth.
vendors.address: 4343 Ocean View Blvd, San Diego, CA 92113
vendors.hours: Office Mon-Thu 9am-8pm, Fri 9am-3pm. Performance times vary by production.

vendors.name: San Diego Black Film Festival
vendors.tagline: Annual showcase of Black and diaspora cinema
vendors.description: Founded in 2002, SDBFF is one of the largest Black film festivals in the country, screening more than 100 features, documentaries and shorts each year across San Diego theaters. The five day event runs during the last week of January with panel discussions, filmmaker mixers and an awards gala.
vendors.address: 3555 Rosecrans St, Suite 114-215, San Diego, CA 92110
vendors.hours: Festival runs annually in late January. Office by appointment.

vendors.name: San Diego African American Museum of Fine Arts
vendors.tagline: A museum without walls for Black fine art
vendors.description: SDAAMFA presents and preserves the fine art of African Americans and the wider diaspora, operating by design as a museum without walls rather than from a permanent gallery. Founded in 1992 and revived in 2014 under Executive Director Gaidi Finnie, it mounts exhibitions with partner venues and runs the annual Keepers of the Culture honors.
vendors.hours: No permanent gallery. Exhibitions hosted at partner venues.

vendors.name: Casa del Rey Moro African Museum
vendors.tagline: 6,000 years of African history in Old Town
vendors.description: Founded by Chuck Ambers, this Old Town museum traces roughly 6,000 years of African and diaspora history with an emphasis on African Spanish, African Mexican and African American heritage. Alongside artifacts from more than ten African nations it houses a research center of some 6,000 books in nine languages, a gift shop and a heritage tour program.
vendors.hours: Daily 10:30am-7pm. Small volunteer run museum, call ahead.

vendors.name: WorldBeat Cultural Center
vendors.tagline: African diaspora and Indigenous culture in Balboa Park
vendors.description: Housed in a repurposed Balboa Park water tower since 1996 and led by founder Makeda Dread Cheatom, this nonprofit celebrates African diaspora and Indigenous world cultures through concerts, drum and dance classes, exhibits and festivals. It also runs the George Washington Carver Ethnobotany Peace Garden, a vegan cafe, and annual Kwanzaa and Global Earth Day celebrations.
vendors.hours: Fri-Sun 11am-5pm, closed Mon-Thu. Event nights vary.

events.title: The Meditations Live In Concert
events.description: Jamaican roots reggae pioneers The Meditations perform their harmony driven classics, with San Diego's Raiz Music opening.

events.title: Give Thanks & Praise: Kabaka Pyramid Live
events.description: Grammy winning Jamaican artist Kabaka Pyramid headlines a Thanksgiving week concert blending roots, dancehall and hip hop.

events.title: 4th International Moringa Symposium
events.description: Four day international gathering on moringa science, regenerative agriculture and community led sustainability, the first US edition of the symposium.

vendors.name: Manuelita Brown
vendors.tagline: Bronze sculptor of Black history and everyday dignity
vendors.description: An award winning San Diego County sculptor who left a career teaching mathematics in 2000 to work in bronze full time, making figurative and portrait pieces that reflect the strength of African survivors in the Americas. Her public works include the Sojourner Truth statue at UC San Diego, Stepping Beyond at the Southeast Live Well Center, and the dolphin fountain figures at UTC.

vendors.name: Martin Luther King Jr. Promenade
vendors.tagline: Downtown linear park honoring Dr. King
vendors.description: A 12 acre linear park running about three quarters of a mile along Harbor Drive from the Gaslamp Quarter toward Seaport Village, dedicated in 1992. Its brick walkway is lined with palm allees, some thirty plaques inscribed with Dr. King's words, and public sculpture including Melvin Edwards' Breaking of the Chains. It hosts the annual Martin Luther King Day Celebration each January.
vendors.address: 326 W Harbor Dr, San Diego, CA 92101

vendors.name: Chef Budda Blasian Soul Food
vendors.tagline: Soul food with Blasian flair in Oak Park
vendors.description: A counter service soul food restaurant that grew out of a popular San Diego food truck and opened as a brick and mortar in June 2025. Owners Michael Price and Lily Nachampasak serve fried wings, catfish, shrimp and baked mac alongside rice and gravy, candied yams and greens, plus Lao and Thai dishes reflecting the family's Black and Asian roots. Catering and the original truck still run alongside the storefront.

vendors.name: Surf & Soul Spot
vendors.tagline: Seafood and soul plates, two menus a week
vendors.description: A takeout spot on El Cajon Blvd from Chef Sarajevo Amor Petty with co-owner Sergio Bailey II. It runs two rotating menus: a seafood leaning Surf lineup earlier in the week, then a Soul menu of fried catfish, wings, pork chops, collard greens, candied yams and banana pudding on Friday and Saturday until it sells out.
vendors.address: 7229 El Cajon Blvd, San Diego, CA 92115
vendors.hours: Mon-Wed 11am-7pm Surf menu, Fri-Sat 12pm until sold out Soul menu, closed Thu and Sun

vendors.name: EDEN San Diego
vendors.tagline: Boutique plant nursery and gift shop
vendors.description: A family run boutique nursery and gift shop on Park Blvd in University Heights, open since 2017 as a sister store to North Park Nursery. Inventory spans houseplants, succulents, cacti, air plants, pots and locally made gifts, and the team also takes on interior and exterior plant design, delivery, installation and garden maintenance.

vendors.name: Sandalwood Skin
vendors.tagline: Custom facials, lash lifts and brow lamination
vendors.description: An appointment only skincare studio in North Park run by Natasha, a licensed esthetician trained at the Christine Valmy International School of Esthetics in New York. Treatments are built around each client's concerns, from dehydration and congestion to sensitivity and aging, and include 60 minute custom facials, lash lifts with tint and brow lamination.

vendors.name: Arts-Rec (Barrio Logan)
vendors.tagline: Skate, sneakers and streetwear on Logan Ave
vendors.description: A skate shop and boutique opened in 2018 by longtime professional skateboarder Kellen James. The Logan Ave original stocks hardware from Independent, Spitfire, Baker and Santa Cruz alongside apparel and footwear from Stussy, Nike SB, Vans and Carhartt WIP, and the shop regularly puts on skate jams, art shows and youth fundraisers.

vendors.name: Arts-Rec (Chula Vista)
vendors.tagline: Third Avenue skate shop and streetwear boutique
vendors.description: The second Arts-Rec location, opened in 2021 on Third Avenue in downtown Chula Vista, extending Kellen James's skate shop into the South Bay. It carries the same mix of decks, trucks and wheels plus sneakers and streetwear, and takes part in the shop's skate jams, art shows and local collaborations.

vendors.name: Finesse Products
vendors.tagline: San Diego skate, art and lifestyle brand since 1997
vendors.description: A San Diego skateboard, art and lifestyle brand started in 1997 by brothers Steven and Rod James, with artwork and graphics drawn by Steven and inspired by anime, video games and comics. The line covers decks, apparel, accessories and art prints, including licensed collaborations, and is carried by national skate retailers.

vendors.name: Furlicious Pet Services
vendors.tagline: Mobile dog walking, sitting and bond based training
vendors.description: A mobile San Diego County dog care company offering dog walking, pet sitting and bond based training for dogs of any age or breed using positive reinforcement. Staff are certified in K9 CPR and pet first aid, the business is licensed, bonded and insured, and it also runs group pack hikes and a training academy.

vendors.name: Puzzle Pieces Marketing
vendors.tagline: Nonprofit branding, web design and social
vendors.description: A San Diego marketing agency founded in 2009 by Angel Mason Broadus and co-owned with Kristine Mason Broadus, working mainly with nonprofits and mission driven organizations on branding, website design and development, graphic design, copywriting and social media. The company describes itself as Black owned, women owned, LGBTQ owned and veteran owned.

vendors.name: Dancing Around The Oak Tree Art Studio
vendors.tagline: Inclusive art classes for artists of all abilities
vendors.description: A San Diego nonprofit started by Vickie Lawrence in 2014 that gives people with intellectual and developmental disabilities a supportive place to learn painting, drawing, mixed media and crafts. Vickie is an artist with disabilities herself, and instruction emphasizes both art skills and coping skills, with participants' finished pieces offered for sale through the studio's online shop.
vendors.hours: Programs run at partner sites and online, by appointment

_excluded.name: Hammond's Gourmet Ice Cream (North Park)
_excluded.reason: Permanently closed after service on September 8, 2024, reported as the brand's last remaining San Diego location. The hammondsgourmet.com domain now serves a Honolulu shop only.

_excluded.name: Hammond's Gourmet Ice Cream (Point Loma)
_excluded.address: 3740 Sports Arena Blvd, Suite 6, San Diego, CA 92110
_excluded.reason: Permanently closed, before the North Park location. Marked closed on Yelp.

_excluded.name: StreetCar Merchants of Fried Chicken, Doughnuts & Coffee
_excluded.reason: Permanently closed in 2023. The space is now Happy Medium under unrelated ownership. The former owner was later sentenced in a federal COVID relief and tax fraud case, so this listing carries reputational risk as well as being defunct.

_excluded.name: Suckerfree Southern Plate & Bar
_excluded.reason: Permanently closed in late summer 2022. Smokin J's BBQ took over the Gaslamp space. Same ownership as StreetCar Merchants.

_excluded.name: Shotcaller Street Soul Food
_excluded.address: 220 Euclid Ave, Suite 180, San Diego, CA 92114
_excluded.reason: Permanently closed by mid-2024. The Po'Boy Shop opened in the space. Same ownership as StreetCar Merchants.

_excluded.name: Hey Sugar!
_excluded.reason: No longer operating in San Diego. The East Village and Old Town locations are gone and the business now trades from Murrieta in Riverside County, outside the shell's geography.

_excluded.name: Sew Forgiven Artisan House
_excluded.reason: Could not verify as operating or as San Diego based. sewforgiven.com returns HTTP 500, the Shop storefront lists no products, and the owner's vendor profile now lists Hemet, CA with no activity since February 2025.

_excluded.name: Trust Restaurant Group (Trust, Fort Oak, Cardellino, Rare Society, The Wise Ox, A L'ouest)
_excluded.address: 3752 Park Blvd, San Diego, CA 92103 and others
_excluded.reason: All locations are open and thriving, but Black ownership could not be confirmed at source. Founder and owner Brad Wise and the named partners are listed on the group's own site with no ownership demographic stated anywhere in their materials or press. Third party directories (Intentionalist, SanDiegoVille, buyblack.org) tag the group as Black owned but none discloses a verification method. Confirm directly with info@trustrgsd.com before listing. Current roster is Trust, Fort Oak, Cardellino, Carlo, Rare Society (University Heights and Solana Beach in county), The Wise Ox (North Park and Carlsbad), Wild Child Ice Cream, and A L'ouest which opened February 11, 2026 in North Park.

_excluded.name: Polishd n' Poppin Nails
_excluded.reason: Could not verify as currently operating. The Acuity booking page still loads but the polishdnpoppinnails.com shop domain no longer resolves, no street address is published beyond 'Imperial Ave', and no public activity from 2025 or 2026 was found. Nothing to pin and nothing to confirm. Re-check before seeding.

_research_notes._method: Every entry was researched independently on September 11, 2026 against the business's own site first, then listing pages, local press and social accounts. Coordinates come from the US Census Bureau geocoder (geocoding.geo.census.gov, Public_AR_Current) or from published map data, cross checked where possible. Nominatim blocks automated fetches. No coordinates were invented. Nothing was copied verbatim from either source list.
_research_notes.chula-vista-brewery: The second Eastlake location at 871 Showroom Place permanently closed in August 2026 when its lease expired; operations consolidated to Third Avenue, so only one entry exists. A 45 day ABC license suspension ran October 2 to November 16, 2025 and is long over. Weekly programming (Comedy Run Club Thursdays, Vinyl Fridays 8pm) is recurring with no published dates, so events is empty rather than fabricated.
_research_notes.muzita-abyssinian-bistro: Hours taken from muzita.net. OpenTable shows materially different hours but its data looks stale, with newest reviews from 2015 and bookings disabled. The site publishes a personal looking Gmail address as its contact; I left email blank rather than put it in a public directory. Confirm with the owner if you want it listed.
_research_notes.coops-west-texas-bbq: The storefront closed in March 2024 and reopened on a weekend only schedule. Stale search results still report it as closed after 13 years, so expect that question. KPBS (February 2025) and the official site both confirm Fri-Sun 10am-3pm at the Lemon Grove address.
_research_notes.mayas-cookies: The source article's street number, 4670 Mission Gorge Pl, is wrong. The correct address is 4760 Mission Gorge Pl, Suite G. A second store operates at 250 North City Drive, Suite 8, San Marcos, (760) 290-3032, Tue-Sun 1pm-9pm. I left San Marcos out because the Census geocoder returned no match for that address; add it as its own entry once you have a confirmed pin.
_research_notes.one-worldbeat-cafe: The cafe sits inside WorldBeat Cultural Center and shares its phone. Its events array is deliberately empty so center programming is not duplicated across two cards; all of it lives on worldbeat-cultural-center.
_research_notes.kebab-craft: CAVEAT: Black ownership is asserted only by the sandiego.org article. The company's own About page names owners Shannon and Paul and says nothing about ownership demographics. Confirm before publishing. Also note a second location in San Juan Capistrano, outside the shell geography.
_research_notes.lili-kouture: CAVEAT: could not confirm the storefront is currently open. Both domains (lilikouture.com, lkfashiondesign.com) no longer resolve, and the Etsy shop reads 'LiliKouture is currently not selling on Etsy.' The address still appears on Yelp and in MTS's Black owned business guide but nothing from 2025 or 2026 confirms it is trading. Coordinates geocoded fresh from the Census geocoder. Call before publishing.
_research_notes.fivespace: CAVEAT: conflicting signals. The online shop is live with inventory dated into late 2025, but Google derived listings show the University Ave storefront as permanently closed and Black Directory lists it as temporarily closed, while Discogs still shows daily noon to 5pm hours. Hours field says walk in unconfirmed. Verify before showing the map pin.
_research_notes.reggae-world: Website left blank on purpose: both domains associated with the shop (reggaworld.com, reggaemadnessmusic.com) fail to load. No Instagram could be confirmed as belonging to this shop rather than unrelated reggae media accounts. Open status comes from consistent daily hours across multiple current directories and a Yelp page refreshed September 2026.
_research_notes.common-ground-theatre: Weakest active signal of the cultural entries. Site is live with current contact details and 62nd season content through June 2026, but no 2026-27 season is posted and the ticket link still points to a 2025 production. sandiego.org lists a stale alternate site (cgtsd.org) and phone (619) 272-3209; the numbers above are the current official ones. Phone verification recommended.
_research_notes.san-diego-black-film-festival: The 2026 edition ran January 28 to February 1, 2026. The site now says 'We'll see you in 2027' and the 2027 call for submissions is open, but dates and venues are still TBA, so events is empty. The address is a suite mailbox office, not a visitable venue; screenings rotate across San Diego theaters. Consider suppressing the map pin for this entry.
_research_notes.san-diego-african-american-museum-of-fin: No permanent gallery by design, confirmed by a February 2026 KPBS feature quoting Executive Director Gaidi Finnie. Address and coordinates are correctly empty. Its most recent exhibition, San Diego's Lost Neighborhoods, closed May 31, 2026.
_research_notes.casa-del-rey-moro-african-museum: The source article misspells this as 'Casa del Ray Moro.' Correct spelling is Rey. Small volunteer run museum, so posted hours are not always reliable; most recent visitor review dates to November 2025.
_research_notes.worldbeat-cultural-center: Date conflict on Kabaka Pyramid: the center's calendar widget shows November 25 but both the event description and the Humanitix ticket page say Tuesday November 24, 2026, and November 24 is in fact a Tuesday. Used November 24. The Moringa Symposium also came back as October 2026 in one pass and October 2027 in another; the event page reads October 6 to 9, 2027, which is what is used here. Verify both against the center before the cards go live.
_research_notes.manuelita-brown: The source article misspells her name as 'Manueltia.' Correct spelling is Manuelita. Wikipedia cites manuelitabrown.com, which does not resolve; her live official site is tsahaistudio.com. Her studio is in Encinitas, North County, outside San Diego city limits. Flagging in case the shell has a geographic boundary.
_research_notes.martin-luther-king-jr-promenade: No official City of San Diego page exists for the promenade, so website is empty. 326 W Harbor Dr is the commonly listed civic address near the west end; Wikipedia gives the park centroid as 32.7089, -117.1632 if you prefer a mid park pin. The annual MLK Day celebration is referenced in the description but no dated event was added because recent city MLK Day events have been held at the MLK Recreation Center in Skyline, not on the promenade.
_research_notes.chef-budda-blasian-soul-food: Started as a sidewalk and food truck operation and opened the 54th St storefront in June 2025. Address on the DoSD list is correct. Online ordering is live and the business vended at San Diego Pride in July 2026.
_research_notes.surf-and-soul-spot: The DoSD list says La Mesa but gives a San Diego address. The San Diego address is right: 92115 sits just west of the La Mesa line, inside city limits. The name is singular, Surf & Soul Spot, not Spots. Two different menus run on different days, which is why the hours string is unusual.
_research_notes.eden-san-diego: CAVEAT: conflicting signals. The business site and events calendar are live with Thu-Sun hours, but two separate Yelp listings for 4636 Park Blvd are flagged closed as of July 2026 and no news source settles it. Phone confirm before publishing.
_research_notes.sandalwood-skin: The DoSD list's zip is wrong. 3959 30th St is North Park, 92104, not 92109, and the suite is 103C rather than 103. Corrected here. Appointment only via Square booking.
_research_notes.arts-rec-barrio-logan: Founded 2018 by pro skater Kellen James. The shop's own pages list slightly inconsistent hours between the store page and the footer, so confirm before publishing.
_research_notes.arts-rec-chula-vista: Second location, opened 2021. Listed with full hours on its own store page and in the Downtown Chula Vista merchant directory, but the site's store-locations index page lists only Barrio Logan, so worth a call. Outside San Diego city limits.
_research_notes.finesse-products: Online and wholesale only, no storefront, so address and pin are intentionally empty. Current season decks are stocked by Zumiez, Skate Warehouse and Warehouse Skateboards, which is the strongest signal the brand is active.
_research_notes.furlicious-pet-services: Mobile and in home service with no public storefront, so address and pin are intentionally empty. The LLC's only registered address is a Poway residence and is deliberately not published here. California LLC registration is active and the BBB profile shows operation since 2019. BBB lists an alternate phone of (858) 746-9591.
_research_notes.puzzle-pieces-marketing: Address deliberately left empty. The Hazard Center address on the DoSD list is a PostalAnnex mailbox and is also stale; the agency's current published address, 5694 Mission Center Rd Suite 602-958, is a UPS Store mailbox. Neither is a visitable office, so neither should become a map pin. Phone is area code 858, not 619. The company also self-asserts SBA Women-Owned, Veteran-Owned and Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned certifications, which were not independently checked in SAM.gov. LinkedIn: linkedin.com/company/puzzle-pieces-marketing.
_research_notes.dancing-around-the-oak-tree-art-studio: CAVEAT on two fronts. Address deliberately left empty: 1050 B St Unit 519 is an apartment in the Ten Fifty B residential tower, almost certainly the founder's home, so it must not be published as a visitable studio. And the open status is the weakest in the file: the site is live and Facebook is linked from its own contact page, but every item in the online shop shows unavailable and the most recent independent confirmation is a September 2025 grant write up. The phone number comes from the East Village directory rather than the studio itself. Call before publishing. Category could reasonably be Nonprofit instead of Arts; 501(c)(3) status could not be confirmed.
